# OMP model UI reference frames

These are display-cell captures from the installed **OMP 18.14.2** binary,
not snapshots generated by the Go renderer. The picker files contain only the
bottom sheet; manager files contain the whole fullscreen frame. Trailing spaces
inside the JSON strings are intentional: they record exact padding and borders.

Captured with real PTYs at 120×40 and 80×24 using:

```sh
python3 scripts/compare-model-tuis.py \
  --omp /path/to/omp --slim ./bin/ompig-slim \
  --output /tmp/model-ui-120x40
python3 scripts/compare-model-tuis.py \
  --omp /path/to/omp --slim ./bin/ompig-slim \
  --output /tmp/model-ui-80x24 --columns 80 --rows 24
```

The script creates isolated profiles, registers two identical loopback-only
fixture models, and disables unrelated providers in both runtimes. Model scopes
are not used; the host supports only role-based selection. It sends menu keys,
never model prompts. It requires the optional Python `pyte` package; ordinary
Go tests and `make smoke` do not.

For all seven views, the script compares display text and foreground/background/
bold on nonblank cells. ANSI streams and complete cell maps remain in the output
directory for inspection. The Go golden tests protect the same text geometry
without depending on Python or an installed OMP binary.

Catalog isolation matters: the production PiG and OMP catalogs expose different
model kinds, and this visual fixture does not establish transport/backend parity.
Presets remain deliberately removed from this port. Update reference files only
from reviewed OMP captures, not from failing Go test output.
